articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Wire Sizing for Low-Voltage Three- Phase Systems in Direct Current Fast Charging (DCFC) Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The global push towards sustainability is propelled by concerted efforts among world leaders to reduce GHG emissions and promote green energy in transportation. Electric vehicles (EVs) play a crucial role in this shift, highlighting the need for a robust and dependable EV charging infrastructure. This paper delves into the critical aspect of wire sizing within electrical power systems, encompassing transformers, energy meters, relays, fuses, and other essential components relevant to DC fast charger infrastructure. Specifically, it explores the design considerations for DC fast chargers and addresses scenarios where undersized wires can compromise operational efficiency. The study introduces a comprehensive framework for optimizing wire sizes tailored specifically for DC fast chargers, offering insights that extend to various other wire sizing applications. Emphasizing adherence to optimal parameters is crucial to en-sure safe and efficient operation, in line with industry standards and operational demands.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network for Microhydro Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The demand for electrical energy is always fluctuating, influenced by several factors such as household, industrial, commercial, and other public service electricity usage. Moreover, estimates of future electricity demand play a crucial role in the operation of the power system, ranging from power generation planning to power flow analysis and energy system operation costs. Electrical power forecasting aims to prevent sudden decreases or increases in electricity demand. Moreover, in tropical countries, the wet season and rivers offer many opportunities for micro-hydro potentials that can be harnessed in combination with solar energy. To manage the forecasting modeling, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is utilized CNN for short-term forecasting in Microhydro Power Plants. The anticipated outcomes aim to contribute to effective electricity demand management, facilitating the estimates of variation in microhydro power generation.

articleTitle: Standalone Photovoltaic Lithium-Ion Battery System with Sinusoidal-Ripple-Current Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The integration of solar photovoltaic (PV) into Electric Vehicle (EV) charging systems has witnessed a notable surge, driven by its clean, and low-pollution attributes. With EVs often parked idle during the daytime, the roofing of parking areas with PV panels offers an opportunity for ‘charging while parking’, presenting an economical solution for parking zones. Lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries stand as the predominant choice for EVs. The Sinusoidal-ripple-current (SRC) method stands out as the primary charging approach when compared to conventional methods. Its zero-time feature enhances battery lifespan. However, in SRC charging, the PV system does not supply energy during the zero period, leading to unused energy in standalone PV battery systems. To maximize PV energy utilization and minimize battery charging time, efficient control strategies for standalone PV-Li-ion battery systems are proposed. Analysis indicates that out-of-phase converter operation with SRC charging is an effective strategy for faster charging and optimized PV utilization.

articleTitle: Carbon Neutral University: A Case Study from Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Higher Education Institutions worldwide aim to achieve carbon neutrality. This study examined the path to carbon neutrality for a university by evaluating the baseline greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and identifying unavoidable emissions after the implementation of all mitigation projects. These projects were assumed to be implemented shortly, both technically and financially. The evaluation followed national guidelines from the Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organization, aligned with ISO 14064–1 (2018) and the GHG Protocol (2001, 2004). Mitigation initiatives included energy efficiency, renewable energy, and transitioning from Internal Combustion Engine to Electric Vehicle projects. Numerical results showed that Scope I and Scope II emissions totaled 5,330.55 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{tCO}_{2}$</tex>-eq in 2023, with contributions from vehicle fuel combustion (39.21 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{tCO}_{2}$</tex>-eq), refrigerant leakage (1,829.53 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{tCO}_{2}{-}$</tex> eq), and purchased electricity (3,461.81 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{tCO}_{2}$</tex>-eq). Implementing all projects could reduce emissions by 1,078.40 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{tCO}_{2}$</tex>-eq. The remaining unavoidable emissions could be offset by purchasing carbon credits or renewable energy certificates.

articleTitle: Financial Analysis of Cooling Systems for Environmental Conditioned Strawberry Cultivation in Semi-Closed Greenhouses in Chiang Mai, Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Strawberry production is an important crop in the northern region of Thailand that is only available in winter. Theoretically, strawberries can be grown in plant factories that can control the climate conditions strawberries need. Generally, the cooling load from lighting accounts for almost 80% of the total heat load in the plant factory. To reduce the cost of using light energy and the heat load in plant factories, this study was conducted on cultivation methods in semi-closed greenhouses that utilize natural light during the day. Coolness is generated by solar energy during the day and stored in cooling energy storage that stored coolness is used during the night. The total cooling load for year-round strawberry cultivation in the greenhouse was about 814 GJ, consisting of the stages of strawberry floral initiation, flowering, and fruiting at 17%, 17%, and 66%, respectively. In addition, the payback period is around 14.16 - 16.29 years.

articleTitle: Power Flow Control and Mode-Switching Method Considering Single-Pole Trip for Bipolar MTDC System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Due to the advantage of the system operation reliability and flexibility, the bipolar multi-terminal high voltage dc (MTDC) transmission has attracted worldwide attention for the integration of offshore windfarms. However, majority of existing operation methods and dc power flow algorithms are designed to control the monopolar MTDC system. It is difficult to implement the conventional control method for the monopolar system into the bipolar system due to the difference in the characteristics of dc power flow control scheme between the two configurations. Therefore, this paper proposes an operation method of the bipolar MTDC system composed of the dc power flow control scheme and mode-switching method. As a simulation result, the proposed method can realize the power sharing between each VSC and reduce the impact of the active power fluctuation on the AC grid connected to the system even when the single-pole trip occurs in the bipolar MTDC system.

articleTitle: Exploring PyPSA for Load Flow Analysis using an IEEE Test Bus Study and Optimization Emphasis using a Modified IEEE Test Bus on PV Integration and Sector Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The increasing utilization of distributed energy resources (DER), particularly solar and wind power generation, alongside the deployment of energy storage and changing demand patterns due to the electrification of transport and industrial heating sectors, are not only causing electricity demand to rise but also leading to stochastic dynamics in power flow patterns. This paper demonstrates the utilization of PyPSA (Python for Power System Analysis) for load flow analysis and optimization for handling time-varying solar PV generation and sector coupling. A comparison of load flow analysis between PyPSA and MATPOWER is conducted using standard IEEE test buses of 9 buses. Additionally, a case study of modified IEEE test bus is presented, showcasing the optimization of an energy system with time-series data of solar PV, load, conventional generation, and integration with transport and heat sectors. The findings demonstrate that load flow analysis produces excellent results for each branch. In addition, the lowest costs for electricity and heat demand can also be obtained by power generation on supply and heat production.

articleTitle: Advancements and Challenges in Nuclear Power Systems for Future Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Nuclear power stands as a crucial cornerstone in the global pursuit of sustainable energy solutions, offering immense potential to mitigate climate change and meet rising energy demands. This paper explores the evolving landscape of nuclear power systems, focusing on innovations, advancements, and challenges shaping their role in the future energy mix. From next-generation reactor designs to advanced fuel cycles and safety technologies, the quest for safer, more efficient, and cost-effective nuclear power generation is underway. However, alongside these advancements, persistent challenges such as nuclear waste management, proliferation risks, and public perception necessitate comprehensive analysis and proactive strategies. Through a multidisciplinary lens encompassing technological, environmental, economic, and social dimensions, this paper aims to provide insights into the trajectory of nuclear power systems and their potential contributions to a sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Wind Power Potential Assessment by Optimization Algorithms at Offshore and Coastal Sites using Reanalysis Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Accurately assessing wind resources is vital for wind energy projects, this study proposes a methodology for evaluates wind resources at coastal and offshore locations in India through Weibull distribution parameter optimization. Employing a 22-year dataset from NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis, wind characteristics are analysed at a 50-meter height using the Weibull probability distribution. Three numerical techniques (Modified Maximum Likelihood Method, Empirical Method of Lysen, and Method of Moment) and two metaheuristic optimization algorithms (Particle Swarm Optimization and Genetic Algorithm) determine shape and scale parameters. Goodness of fit tests, RMSE, and MBE assess method accuracy. Results indicate Modified Maximum Likelihood Method as the most accurate for wind potential evaluation. The offshore wind industry's expansion necessitates reliable predictions, making this research crucial for estimating India's offshore wind resource using reanalysis data. Three numerical approaches are applied, with Maximum Likelihood Method standing out as the most precise for determining wind potential. The study contributes valuable insights into probabilistic modelling of wind resources and MERRA-2 utility. The findings underscore the role of early information in determining the feasibility of wind energy generation at specific coastal and offshore locations in India, providing a foundation for future offshore wind industry developments.

articleTitle: MCDM Approach to Offshore Wind Farm Site Selection in Indian EEZ Considering Climate Change
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This paper focuses at the use of Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methodologies for optimal wind farm site selection in India. The study examines possible sites using a systematic process that incorporates the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and comprises data from stakeholder interactions, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and remote sensing. In this study, wind speeds from climate model's ensemble are used to assess the influence of climate change on the suitability of identified regions. A comparison of selected regions under historical, near future, and far future scenarios is performed. The application of these methodologies is analyzed within Indian EEZ. The results show that 19% of the total study area falls under class 4 and class 5 categories, which are suitable for wind farm installation. In the near future, there is a 2% and 4% improvement in the selected regions under RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5 scenarios, respectively, compared to historical period.

articleTitle: Energy Transition: A Case of Social Resistance from the Community in the Development of Gelun River Hydro Power Development in Nepal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Nepal has a massive potential to harness more than 72,000 MW of hydropower energy by taking advantage of its major river basins and subbasins. Despite having this potential to advance the country's renewable source of energy, Nepal still relies on traditional biomass energy. Through a case study methodology, the paper explores how Gelun River Hydropower Project was initially resisted by the community members along with its influential and local political leaders. The study has used Focus Group Discussion and literature reviews to explore the causes of resistance through the lens of the project developers. The Findings revealed that the community people are unwilling to sell their land for the project as they consider it as an ancestral asset and even if they do they tend to over value the land prices. This creates a hesitance from the community, thus leading to the barriers in the further development of the project.

articleTitle: Assessing Municipal Solid Waste Management Policies and Challenges in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Waste management is always one of the significant issues in Thailand, as the data shows that around a third of the municipal waste is not treated sanitarily. Thus, the regulation framework relating to municipal waste management in Thailand could potentially be one of the challenges causing difficulties in developing sustainable waste management in Thailand. The waste management regulation was initiated under the Ministry of Public Health 32 years ago; a better-related ministry, such as the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment, was established 3 years later. Thus, even until now, the authorization has remained with the Ministry of Public Health. Nevertheless, the ministry that is managing the waste is the Ministry of Interior, which tends to have limited knowledge regarding environmental management. Thus, removing the limitation of the policy framework by giving full authority and reforming the Ministry of Interior could support waste management in Thailand.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach for Appliances Energy Prediction using Differential Evolution Optimization and Light GBM Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This study presents a new method for assessing the energy use of appliances in a low energy residence with the goal of improving energy consumption predictions. Information was collected at 10-minute intervals throughout a period of 137 days. The collected data includes a wide range of equipment, with a specific emphasis on lighting and the relationship between humidity levels and room occupancy. The dataset was divided into three subgroups depending on the lighting feature in order to assess the predictive importance of various parameters: all records, recordings without lighting, and records only including lighting. The suggested investigation employs a hybrid machine learning framework that integrates Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (Light GBM) to forecast energy consumption. In order to improve the precision of the model, a sophisticated differential evolution approach is used to optimize the model's parameters. The models were compared using several performance indicators, such as the mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), coefficient of determination (R2), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). The prediction results showed low error rates and strong correlation coefficients for all of these measurements, highlighting the usefulness of our technique in improving operational efficiency and forecast accuracy in energy management. The combination of bio-inspired optimization algorithms with ensemble machine learning approaches has significant promise for improving energy consumption predictions, which are essential for sustainable home energy management.

articleTitle: Life Cycle Assessment of the Energy Consumption of Olivine Powder Production for Enhanced Weathering using the Mine-to-Mill Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Enhanced weathering, a negative-emissions technology that involves spreading finely grounded silicate rocks to accelerate carbon sequestration, is critical to achieving a net-zero climate future. However, there are concerns related to the uncertainty of the balance of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions to mine, crush, grind, transport, and spread powdered rocks, and the potential carbon dioxide removal. The research aims to estimate the energy consumption across the entire silicate rock powder production chain by utilizing the extraction simulator software to design and model the integrated mine-to-mill process. The analysis scope includes blasting, crushing, primary grinding, and secondary fine grinding. The circuit performance was evaluated for two blasting scenarios: ordinary and intense. The novelty of this study includes the simulation of the entire mine-to-mill process to estimate the specific energy consumption of olivine powder production. This study contributes to the Life Cycle Assessment of technology by improving the scope and accuracy of the analysis.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Rule-Based and Optimization-Based Energy Management for a Campus Microgrid in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: It is challenging to integrate high levels of renewable sources into power distributions systems due to their intermittent nature. Microgrids provide a feasible framework for accommodating higher levels of renewable energy generation while providing other advantages such as improved reliability. However, it is crucial to implement microgrid energy management with proper control methods for the effective utilization of renewable energy and stable operation of the microgrid. Different energy management strategies are employed in microgrids, and the most commonly applied technique in practice is the rule-based energy management, which is the simplest. This article investigates a microgrid pilot project at the University of Moratuwa in Sri Lanka, where the rule-based energy management is in operation. The rule-based energy management strategy is simulated and verified using real data from the microgrid system. Furthermore, an optimization-based method is implemented for the system and the performance metrics of both energy management algorithms are compared.

articleTitle: A Multicriteria Decision Analysis to Selection of Low-carbon Emitting Technologies under Joint Crediting Mechanism for Thailand's Carbon Neutrality 2050
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: To strengthen the global response to the threat of climate change, Parties to the Paris Agreement agree to keep a global temperature rise well below 2-degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels within this century and to pursue efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5-degrees Celsius. Thailand ratified the Paris Agreement in 2016 and pledged its first Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). Subsequently, Thailand's updated NDC 2022 intends to reduce its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 30 percent from the projected business-as-usual (BAU) level by 2030. The level of contribution could increase up to 40 percent, subject to adequate and enhanced access to technology development and transfer, financial resources, and capacity building support of 40% emissions reduction in 2030 compared to its BAU. Presently, Thailand increases its ability to deal with the impacts of climate change and makes the updated NDC consistent with a low GHG emissions and climate-resilient pathways of the Paris Agreement. To reach the ambitious goals, appropriate mobilization and provision of financial resources need to be put in place. The Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) is an important initiative that facilitates collaboration between Japan and partner countries including Thailand to address GHG emissions reduction thru low-emission technologies. The JCM serves as a bridge for global climate action, promoting sustainable development while addressing climate challenges. The bilateral co-operation of JCM between Thailand and Japan was effective since October 13, 2015, and will be ended by December 2030. The JCM credits used to achieved Japan's NDC are based on the proportion of shared investments in the JCM projects. Japan may share the JCM investment as high as 50 percent. This paper proposes a multicriteria decision analysis (MCA) to selection of low-carbon emitting technologies under Thailand-Japan JCM for achievement of Thailand's carbon neutrality 2050. Results indicates five promising categories of JCM projects in Thailand: (i) energy efficiency improvement, (ii) renewable energy and biofuels, (iii) advanced electric devices, (iv) advanced thermal devices, and (v) advanced technologies including hydrogen and carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS). In terms of technological readiness and economics, both energy efficiency improvement and renewable energy measures are found cost effective and suitable for domestic actions while advanced electric devices and advanced thermal devices need JCM framework. The advanced technologies including hydrogen CCS, CCUS and bioenergy with CCS (BECCS) need in-dept assessment for JCM. Thus, the JCM facilitates diffusion of leading decarbonizing technologies and infrastructure as well as implementation of mitigation actions and contributes to sustainable development of Thailand.

articleTitle: Assessment of CO2 Emissions from Crushed Stone Transport for Site Selection of Enhanced Weathering Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: In order to achieve carbon neutrality by 2050, negative emission technologies are required, and enhanced weathering is attracting attention. In this process, rocks are crushed and spread on farmland to fix CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. However, since CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is emitted during the process from rock mining to spreading, it is necessary to clarify the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> reduction effect over the entire life cycle. In this study, a case study focusing on transportation distance and spreading area in Hokkaido, Japan has been conducted to evaluate CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission reductions. The area of farmland and the transportation distance from the quarry to the farmland were calculated using Geographic Information System (GIS). The relationship between transportation distance and farmland area was analyzed to clarify the characteristics of each quarry. From the result of the case study, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions from transportation account for up to 30% of total emissions. Furthermore, the quarry case also shows a reduction in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions.

articleTitle: A Proposed Framework for Fuel Chain Total Energy and GHG Analysis for Global Applications Constructed on Leontief Input-Output Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The energy and fuel supply chain of various countries and power mix could vary substantially from one country to another. These distinctions lead to differences in energy requirements and environmental impacts emanating from the extraction, production and transport phases of fuel and energy utilization in countries through-out the world. Considering that energy and fuel supply chain among countries are complexly connected, supply chain and power mix variations in one country could well have significant changes in the sustainability of energy use in another country. If inadequately analyzed, assumptions taken on this issue could be detrimental to the outcomes of environmental assessment of systems. The paper provides a simplified framework based on the Leontief Input-Output economic model that may be used to simultaneously quantify the net energy and GHG production of power and fuels of countries globally. An example involving interactions between three countries is provided to demonstrate the methodology.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Wingsails as Propulsion Power Assistance to the Contribution of Energy Efficiency and Decarbonization: Case of a 6500-Ton DWT Tanker Ship with Different Sail Arrangements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The Paris Agreement, led by the UNFCCC, targets limiting global temperature rise to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. In response, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) aims for zero emissions from maritime transport by the early 2100s. IMO introduced the Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI) for new ships in 2013 and the Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) in 2023, alongside the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) to monitor emissions. Installing wind-powered propulsion is one method suggested for compliance. This study focuses on achieving EEXI and CII compliance using wind assistance, examining wingsail retrofitting on a 6,500-tonne DWT tanker in Indonesia. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models are employed to predict thrust and drag based on wind conditions. Annual energy savings for different sail configurations are evaluated using published wind data, allowing for a comparison of savings versus capital costs to assist ship owners in decision-making.

articleTitle: Circular Carbon Economy of CCUS Application in Thailand's Industries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Currently, several <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> utilization technologies are in the laboratory, prototype, and pilot phases, but some have been fully commercialized. Therefore, this study aims at investigation of the opportunity of Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) technologies deployed in Thai industries in term of long-life carbon utilization products. In this paper, based on high technology readiness level as in the commercial stage, products that have the potential to deploy CCUS technology in a circular carbon economy, especially for utilization in the form of permanent storage in products and having the potential to utilize carbon dioxide in the production of products to support Thailand's net zero greenhouse gas emissions targets consisting of methanol, polyurethane and polycarbonate. Results of the assessment of the potential from the production volume and carbon used in the production of the three types of primary products, indicate that “the use of CCUS technology in the industries producing all three types of primary products have a potential to reduce greenhouse gases in the chemical industry by 1.22 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MtCO}_{2}$</tex> in 2022”. Nevertheless, even if the technology is currently in the commercial stage, its cost is still high. The incentives mechanisms are needed to motivate manufacturers to adopt CCUS technology. Therefore, Thailand can achieve carbon neutrality target by 2050.

articleTitle: Smart Power Optimization in Existing Electric Vehicle Charging Station with Solar Energy and Energy Storage Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Electric vehicles represent the future of transportation. As the number of EVs increases, the level of Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) also rises. This necessitates the use of oversized cables, transformers, and protective devices to prevent a specific type of overload in the electrical system. Incorporating solar panels with an energy storage unit (ESU). Above charging station can reduce the transformer's load during peak demand periods. The EV may be charged using PV (Photovoltaic), grid, ESU, or a combination of the three. By doing this, we can offer EV charging continuously and more affordably. An algorithm has been created to ensure that the electric vehicles are charged continuously and that the quality of the power is maintained throughout the process. The total grid power, solar power, and ESU power used during the day are calculated using a Python application. This concept will be useful for load predictions as well.

articleTitle: Modeling and Assessment of Solar Farm Expansion Using RS, GIS and Machine Learning Techniques: Case of Tarlac Province, Philippines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Adoption of renewable energy (RE) sources is crucial for sustainable development due to its low carbon emissions and enhancing energy security. Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems diversify energy sources, increasing market resilience. However, expanding solar farms affects land use and ecosystems. This study identifies solar farm expansion in Tarlac, Philippines, using remote sensing, geographic information system, and machine learning. Results show cropland decreased from 50.19% in 2017 to 47.64% in 2022, with the largest decrease in grassland (−22.3%). Solar power plant (SPP) areas grew by 333.3%, primarily replacing cropland, raising food security concerns. Model simulations predict a 60% increase in SPPs by 2027, boosting power supply but reducing cropland. This study recommends using higher resolution LULC data and more spatial variables for model improvement. Results from this study can help stakeholders in energy and agriculture develop plans to integrate RE in the energy mix while considering its impact on food security.

articleTitle: Climate Change Impact on Wind Energy Potential in Rameshwaram
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Climate change is expected to affect global energy patterns, including renewable energy sources like wind power. Climate models help us understand these changes, but they come with certain difficulty due to their complexity. This study examines future wind characteristics in Rameshwaram using an ensemble of six regional climate models from the CORDEX-SA domain, specifically the Reg <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>M4 model. This study analyzed wind speeds under two climate instances, RCP4.5 and RCP8.5, for different time periods: near-future (up to 2046), mid-future (up to 2073), and far-future (up to 2099). The result shows a gradual increase in wind resources over time. Wind density peaks in July, leading to the highest energy potential during this month. The monsoon season also shows the highest seasonal wind density, while wind energy potential is expected to increases overall from winter to spring and decreases from summer to fall.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Approach to Urban-Block Energy Efficiency Through Building Envelope Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This study evaluates the impacts of urban forms on energy consumption in two distinct urban forms in Bangkok city. The methodology involves setting up urban block models with adjustment of various envelope design scenarios such as window-to-wall ratio, u-value wall, and u-value glass. The energy consumption and solar energy production of 48 designs were performed using the parametric platform Rhino& Grasshopper with microclimate and energy simulation plugins. The energy intensity among urban blocks was analyzed. Results indicated that the high-density area with a small commercial building ratio was the most energy-efficient form, which achieved positive energy consumption. Notably, commercial buildings significantly contributed to urban energy use. Installing high-performance glass and adjusting the window-to-wall ratio significantly reduced energy consumption in commercial buildings by up to 24%, which is a driving factor of low carbon emissions. The findings could be helpful for architects, urban planners, and policymakers to reduce energy use and carbon emissions through strategic urban design.

articleTitle: Sustainable Practices Through Carbon Offset Coins: Incentivizing Green Energy and Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The global volume of greenhouse gases continues to rise, and it has become a challenge to find means of engaging people to participate in the fight against emissions of greenhouse gases. This paper presents the concept of 'Carbon Offset Coins' as a novel policy tool to incentivize sustainable behaviours at the individual level. This policy prompts the people directly to get rewarded for opting for a greener approach, unlike the carbon credit mechanisms that operate at the corporate and national levels. The policy outlines a plan for its implementation, indicating some of the critical factors, such as its tracking methods, earning, and redemption. This can improve current green financing models as well as speed up the transition to the low-carbon economy. This paper assesses the objectives of the policy, its implementation, and its likely impact on every single person's inclination to contribute towards combating international emission levels.

articleTitle: Optimizing Electric Vehicle Charging Schedules: Minimizing Charging Time and Travel Distance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Growing concerns regarding climate change have led to the development of sustainable transportation solutions. Electric vehicles (EVs) offer a promising alternative to traditional combustion engine vehicles due to their efficiency and reduced environmental impact. However, unlike gasoline-powered vehicles, EVs require longer charging times, introducing limitations on charging accessibility and overall travel time. This study addresses these challenges by proposing an EV charging scheduling model to achieve two objectives: minimizing the time spent on EV charging and reducing the travel distance between charging stations and the final destination. Notably, the proposed method is model-free, eliminating the need for data-driven training processes. The model's efficacy is evaluated through a simulation study utilizing a virtual map and real-world charging station data from Bangkok, Thailand. The simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in scheduling efficiency compared to baseline strategies. The proposed approach achieves 208% and 308% charging time reductions compared to the nearest neighbor station (NNS) and earliest start time (EST) policies.

articleTitle: Enhancing Pure Oscillatory Response Motion Performance: Innovative Designs for Semi-Submersible and Catamaran Floating Photovoltaic Systems (FPVs) in Various Sea-State Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: A study approach to the novel design of floating photovoltaic systems has been provided using CFD simulation to determine motion characteristics on irregular waves with the JONSW AP spectrum under various water conditions. The simulation included in the frequency domain, shows that the CFPV model exhibits more stable behavior compared to its alternative model. This is due to the findings that the SFPV model has motion excitation associated with its own RAO against the wave energy spectrum at a frequency of 2.13 rad/sec (SS-2). This leads to a significantly dominant difference in motion quality concerning the significant response motion parameter. The quality difference values can be distinguished as heave with a value of 0.26 meters, roll with a value of 4.19°, and pitch with a value of 1.27°.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Electrical Characterization of Photoelectrochemical Solar Cell of n-CdS-p-Cu2S Electrode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This paper presents fabrication and characterization of p-type Cu2s and n-type CdS semiconductor electrodes for photo-electrochemical solar cell applications. The n-type cadmium sulphide was deposited on glass substrate by chemical bath deposition process at a temperature of 75°C for 2hours. The chemical bath consisted of Cadmium Chloride, Potassium Hydroxide, Ammonium Nitrate and Thiourea with concentration of 0.02M, 0.5M, 1.5M, and 0.2M respectively. The p-type copper (II) sulphide was formed on the CdS layer using a solution consisting of copper chloride. The values obtained for photovoltaic parameters of the photo-electrochemical cell are the short-circuit current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf>) 0.56mA, open-circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>) 0.615V, fill factor (FF) 0.61 and efficiency (q) 0.14%.

articleTitle: Roles of Green Infrastructure in Educational Institutions: A Case Study of Thammasat University Rangsit Campus
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This study investigates the roles of green infrastructure (GI) within Thammasat University Rangsit campus. The objectives include examining the types and roles of existing GI and their impacts on individuals and the university. The study found that the existing GI in the university can be classified into five types and distributed across three main functional zones: service, educational, and residential. The types and roles of GI include 1) green buffer, these spaces separate different functional zones and accommodate various activities; 2) green patch, designed for relaxation, these areas enhance the environment by supporting diverse plant and animal species; 3) green corridor, facilitating non-motorized transportation (walking and cycling), these corridors also enhance the university's aesthetic landscape; 4) green building, Thammasat's buildings prioritize good ventilation and incorporate solar roofs to reduce energy consumption; 5) green canal and river, these areas delineate university territories and functional zones while serving as water drainage channels.

articleTitle: Assessing CO2 Emissions in the Thai Cement Industry and Possible Reductions Through Green Public Procurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The global cement industry accounts for over 7% of global CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. Therefore, decarbonizing this sector is critical to achieving the Paris Climate Agreement goals. Thailand's cement industry is also one of the largest sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the country. This study investigates the CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions from this industry and presents a strategic approach for its decarbonization based on green public procurement (GPP) policy. The procurement of cement for Government-funded projects accounted for 40% of the total amount of cement consumed in Thailand in 2021. This purchasing power gives governments leverage in driving markets toward the production of low-carbon cement. This study considers four GPP scenarios (low, medium, high, transformative) to reduce CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions in Thailand's cement industry. The results show that the annual emission reductions directly derived from government procurement of cement for construction in the country under the four scenarios considered amount to 1.2, 2.5, 3.7, and 6.1 million tonne CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/year, respectively. By developing these scenarios, this research attempts to quantify the impact of GPP policies with different target levels to minimize the carbon footprint associated with cement production in Thailand. Based on international best practices, practical recommendations are provided for the development of a GPP policy for cement in Thailand.

articleTitle: P2P Energy Sharing with Federated Learning and Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This paper presents a peer-to-peer electricity trading framework with dynamic pricing designed to enhance energy availability and economic returns for market participants. A key feature of the proposed model is the use of federated learning for predictive pricing for energy, ensuring data privacy while considering user preferences. Simulation results validate that this approach significantly improves energy availability and financial benefits. The method is implemented on the Ethereum public blockchain, providing a secure and transparent trading environment. Real-world data tests further confirm the efficacy of the system, demonstrating enhanced reliability and economic gains for participants in decentralized energy markets.

articleTitle: Reanalysis of Energy Storage System in Agriculture Greenhouse
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: In the recent agriculture innovation, the integration of smart storage materials such as phase change materials (PCMs) in greenhouse environment stands as a promising frontier. The purpose of PCMs utilization in agriculture greenhouses to conserve energy, temperature regulation, energy efficiency and provide comfortable climates for crop growth and development in greenhouse setting during day and night time. By harvesting of energy in the form of latent heat and release capabilities of PCMs, Smart storage solution can be designed to create more stable and controlled climate condition within agriculture greenhouses. This is not only the mitigates extreme temperature but also enhance the overall productivity and yield of corps. This review content presents the technological advancements and innovations in the field, displaying the real-world implementation and demonstrated the effectiveness of such integrated smart storage system. It aims to provide a comprehensive understanding for current state of smart storage solution in agriculture, unveiling a landscape where innovation converges with climates to cultivate a more resilient and resource efficient future for the agriculture sector.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis and Forecasting of Wind Speed at Khavda Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This study investigates wind speed prediction at Khavda, Gujarat, using machine learning models. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Regression, and Random Forest algorithms were employed for long-term forecasting. The dataset comprised 1,014 entries starting from the year 1940, which included the monthly aggregated wind speeds and directions. Model performance was evaluated using R-squared (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). While all models demonstrated suitability for forecasting, the SVR model proved most efficient with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>value of 0.997, MAE of 0.1841, MSE of 0.0576, and RMSE of 0.2336. This research contributes to enhancing wind power prediction accuracy at Khavda, crucial for efficient grid management and resource allocation in renewable energy systems. The findings support the ongoing shift towards sustainable energy solutions and climate change mitigation efforts.

articleTitle: Pyrolysis Oil Produced from Landfill Waste Plastic with Calcined Fly Ash Catalyst
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This research investigated catalytic pyrolysis fuel oil production from waste plastic sourced from a 10-year-old landfill in Nonthaburi Province. The aim is to study the effect of catalysts on producing pyrolysis fuel oil resembling commercial diesel. A bench-scale fixed bed reactor with an 18.85-liter volume was operated at 450°C, using fly ash waste and calcined fly ash at 600°C and 700°C. The chemical composition of the produced pyrolysis oil was analyzed using Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR) and Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS). Heating values were determined with a bomb calorimeter. The FT-IR spectrum revealed that aliphatic hydrocarbons, especially alkenes, and alkanes, were the main components of the pyrolysis oil. The highest yields were 53.8% from calcined fly ash at 600°C and 37.3% from fly ash at 700°C. The maximum heating value from raw fly ash was 45.77 MJ/kg. The resulting pyrolysis oil can serve as an alternative liquid fuel in industry.

articleTitle: Decarbonization of Power Sector in Thailand to Achieve Carbon Neutrality by 2050
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Thailand has significantly raised its emissions reduction goals, aiming for carbon neutrality by 2050 and setting a net-zero greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions target for 2065. The power sector is the largest contributor to carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) emissions and plays a pivotal role in decarbonizing other sectors. As such, a comprehensive reform and decarbonization of the power sector are imperative for Thailand to successfully achieve the carbon neutrality and net-zero GHG emissions goals. This study hence develops a recursive dynamic Asia-Pacific Integrated Model/Computable General Equilibrium (AIM/CGE) model to analyze the economy-wide impacts of decarbonization pathways focusing on the Thai power sector. In doing so, this study disaggregates the electricity generation sector into various renewable and fossil-based sources when evaluating the responses to decarbonization policies. Simulations indicate that disaggregation in electricity production is important for accurately quantifying the economic impacts of carbon mitigation.

articleTitle: Queueing Theoretical Approach and Markov Modeling Employed in Multiple Charging Stations of Electric Vehicle Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The use of electric automobiles, or rather EVs, represents both an opportunity and a challenge in transportation and energy systems. This study investigates the effectiveness of the number and locations of EV charging stations using Markovian modeling while emphasizing the objective reality of demand growth and the need for a highly developed charging infrastructure. Abandonment, the tendency of individuals to leave a queue because of waiting for a long time, has implications on both system efficiency and individual perception. Thus, this research applies the queueing theoretical approach and stochastic models to improve charging stations through feedback mechanisms and abandonment to control queues. Based on the analysis of various models and charging strategies, this research aims to propose effective solutions for EV charging infrastructure and its associated issues. It provides information that can help improve the services' efficiency and create more effective strategies for the ever-growing EV market.

articleTitle: Innovative Synthesis of Aluminum Oxide Impregnated Carbon Nanotube Membranes for Effective Cr(VI) Removal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: A facile method of synthesizing aluminum oxide-impregnated carbon nanotubes membrane is reported. In the first step, various loadings (1 to 20%) of aluminum oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Al}_{2}\mathbf{O}_{3})$</tex> were impregnated on the surface of multiwall carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs). In the second step, the impregnated MWCNTs were compacted at 200-300MPa and sintered at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1200-1400^{\circ}\mathbf{C}$</tex> to procedure the disk-shaped membrane. The fabricated membranes have the advantage of producing a network of tightly held CNTs that can utilize the excellent properties of nanotubes for applications in water treatment. The fabricated membranes were employed for the removal of Cr(VI) ions from a large volume of water in a continuous filtration setup. The effect of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Al}_{2}\mathbf{O}_{3}$</tex> loadings on the characteristics of the prepared membrane was also evaluated. Membrane with 10% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Al}_{2}\mathbf{O}_{3}$</tex> content exhibited better Cr(VI) ions removal.

articleTitle: Exploration of the Prospects of Wind Energy Systems in Central Province of Saudi Arabia - A Way Forward to Green Future
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This study investigates feasibility (techno-economic) for developing 30MW wind-energy-system (wind-farm) at Riyadh, Central Province, Saudi Arabia (K.S.A) by examining long-term wind-speed-data. The wind-energy resource of Riyadh is reasonable. According to data analysis, monthly-average wind-speeds of Riyadh (24°42‘ N, 46°44’ E) range from 3.0 to 3.9 m/s (at height of 10m). The wind-farms simulations comprised of various mixes of 600 kW commercial wind-machines (60m height-of-hub). Feasibility evaluation was achieved by employing HOMER-Energy's (NREL's) HOMER-software. The outcomes of study presented include monthly wind-speed variations, FD-profiles (frequency-distribution profiles) of wind-speeds, month-by-month and annual quantity of generated-energy from the 30MW-wind-energy-system (60m hub), cost of generation-of-energy (COE, US$-per-kWh), capacity-factor (percent), etc. According to FD-profiles, wind-speeds are under 3m/s for roughly 52 percent duration of a year. This suggests that commercial wind-electric-conversion-systems (WECS) can generate energy (MWh) for roughly 48% duration of a year. About 33395 MWh of energy is produced from 30MW-WECS (with 60m hub-level) every year. The COE by utilization of 600kW (60m hub-level) is roughly 0.0703 US$-per-kWh. With installation of 30MW WECS, approximately 1683 tons emissions (carbon) can be refrained every year. Various other associated factors (e.g. height-of-hub, capacity factor, etc.) for WECS-installation have also been examined.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization of Commercial Airliner Electrical Environmental Control System (EECS) Using Energy Recovery Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The environmental control system (ECS) of an aircraft is vital for maintaining a suitable environment for both cabin and avionics. More Electric Aircraft (MEA) aims to tackle critical issues by increasing energy efficiency by the use of electric power for non-propulsive systems in an aircraft. The electrical power of the compressor can be sourced from either the engine shaft or an independent electrical power source, which has a lower energy cost than that of engine power extraction. This study proposes to enhance the energy efficiency of a commercial aeroplane electric driven ECS (EECS) by incorporating an energy recovery unit that captures energy from the cabin exhaust air. This energy recovery unit compressor aids in the precompression of air before being compressed in electric compressor. This results in less power required for fresh air compression, which saves 35.77% of energy required to run the ECS. Coefficient of performance improved by 25%.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of Two-Wheel Bleed-Less Air Cycle Environment Control System for Aerospace Applications Using Dymola
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The Bleed-less Environment Control System (BECS) plays a crucial role in regulating the environmental conditions within aircraft cabins, ensuring passenger comfort and safety. This paper presents a comprehensive dynamic analysis of the BECS, aiming to enhance understanding of its performance characteristics and identify potential areas for optimization and improvement. Using a combination of computational modeling using commercial software Dymola and MATLAB code validation, this study investigates the dynamic behavior of key components within the BECS, including cold air unit (CAU), compact heat exchangers, and temperature control algorithms. The transient responses of these components for varying operating conditions, such as changes in altitude, ambient temperature, and passenger load, are thoroughly examined. This analysis provides valuable insights into the overall dynamic performance of the BECS, highlighting areas where response times may be optimised to improve system efficiency and reliability. Furthermore, the study explores the impact of different control strategies on system stability and response characteristics, offering recommendations for designing advanced control algorithms tailored to the unique requirements of the BECS. Overall, this research contributes to a deeper understanding of the dynamic behaviour of the BECS and lays the groundwork for future advancements in aircraft environmental control systems, ultimately enhancing passenger comfort and safety during flight. Using the Bleed-less ECS, the aspects of aircraft system energy saving are also discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Use of Hybrid Roughness Elements for the Augmentation of Performance in Solar Air Heaters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The utilization of fossil fuels significantly exacerbates climate change, posing a considerable challenge in the quest for sustainable renewable energy sources essential for a better future. Solar radiation is regarded as a highly advantageous renewable energy resource due to its widespread availability and environmentally sustainable nature. To capture and utilize this energy, solar collectors are employed to transform solar radiation into thermal energy. Nevertheless, inefficient heat transfer can adversely affect their performance. This inefficiency is primarily attributed to the low heat transfer coefficient caused by the formation of a laminar sublayer over the surface, which hinders effective thermal contact between the heated surface and the fluid (air). Disrupting this laminar sublayer is critical for enhancing heat transfer. Artificial roughness is acknowledged as one of the most effective passive techniques for improving the performance of solar air heating systems. Various forms of roughness are applied to the underside of the absorber plate to disrupt the laminar sublayer and induce local turbulence, thereby enhancing heat transfer. While some studies have explored hybrid roughness elements, this research specifically investigates the combination of dimpled and multi-V-shaped gap roughness to evaluate heat transfer and friction characteristics. The findings demonstrate a substantial improvement in heat transfer, with the thermohydraulic performance parameter (TPP) also being assessed to gauge overall system efficiency.

articleTitle: Average Current Control Design of Active Power Decoupling Converter with Low Filter Inductance Based on Double Sampling Techniques for PV Microinverter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Active power decoupling (APD) converter is a power dense and reliable solution in dc-ac power conversion systems to balance the fluctuating ac-side power and constant dc-side power. In boost type APD converter, filter inductor with low inductance can be beneficial in achieving efficient and compact designs or allows the implementation of zero voltage switching (ZVS) based modulation. On the other hand, the reduced inductance increases the difficulty of controller design due to reduction of the average current control loop phase margin and higher requirement in low-pass-filter (LPF). This paper proposes an average current control based on double sampling techniques to reduce the phase delay of LPF and improve the current tracking performance under low inductance. The implementation of double sampling in the digital signal processor (DSP) and the design of control loops are discussed. The proposed approach is experimentally verified using a 40 V, 400 W APD converter prototype.

articleTitle: Carbon Neutral Event: A Case Study from Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This study explored achieving carbon neutrality in event organization, focusing on transportation, energy use, food and beverage, paper usage, and waste management. The Wonder Festival, held at a Thai university in Bangkok on May 2, 2024, attracted 7,528 participants, with 7,153 attending at night and 375 during the day. The event featured 50 booths with food, beverages, and products, along with stage talks, edutainment, and showcases of sustainability research and student projects. GHG emissions were assessed following Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organization (TGO) guidelines, covering Scope 1 (direct emissions), Scope 2 (indirect emissions), and Scope 3 (other indirect emissions). Total emissions were 34.21 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{tCO}_{2}-\text{eq}$</tex>: 9.87% from Scope 1, 3.47% from Scope 2, and 86.65% from Scope 3, mainly from travel and waste. Achieving carbon neutrality requires purchasing carbon credits from the Thailand Voluntary Emission Reduction Program (T-VER), costing 2,082.41 THB. The findings aid university administrators in promoting sustainability initiatives.

articleTitle: Transmitting Efficiency Monotonicity of Multi-LED Optical Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This research presents a theoretical analysis for the transmitting efficiency in the air of optical wireless power transfer (OWPT) systems with transmitters consisting of a light emitting diode (LED) array. Analytical and explicit conditions are derived to characterize the monotonic dependence of the transmitting efficiency on the relative distances between the solar cell optical receiver and the LED array transmitter. As such, the receiver locations to obtain more wirelessly transmitted power can be determined. The usefulness of the derived theoretical formulas is then validated with numerical simulations and experimental results conducted in the laboratory.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Techno-Economic Feasibility of a Solar Electrolysis Hydrogen Refueling Station in Island Environments: A Corsican Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: After the Paris Agreement, which emphasizes the critical need for sustainable solutions to combat climate change, Corsica is actively seeking effective solutions through green hydrogen to ensure its energy transition, with a particular focus on heavy mobility, especially considering that energy costs on islands are higher than on the mainland. Our article presents a comprehensive techno-economic analysis of a hydrogen refueling station for buses, aiming to design a facility capable of producing 440 kg of hydrogen daily through on-site electrolysis of 4.5 MW. The total installation cost (TC) amounted to 22,324,617 Euros. The Levelized Hydrogen Cost (LHC) is calculated at 6.95 Euros per kg of hydrogen over a 20-year lifespan, confirming its cost-effectiveness compared to real case studies for fuel cell buses of the 3Emotion project. Our study also marks the beginning of large-scale hydrogen integration, starting with buses and extending to maritime mobility, contributing significantly to the transition to cleaner and sustainable mobility in islands.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Parameters Leading to Agrivoltaics System Success: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Energy transition mechanisms for achieving net zero to combat climate change is a nationally determined target set by developed countries following the Paris Agreement. Agrivoltaics is considered as an option which can reduce land conflict between agricultural activity and solar power generation. The paper reviews 567 agrivoltaics plants developed by various stakeholders in the United States of America with an objective of identifying factors which led to its success. It has been observed that the climate change policy is a driver for the growth of agrivoltaics in the USA since 2015. Habitat and grazing are two preferred agrivoltaics activities because of its compatibility with existing infrastructure and low economic risk compared to that of crop production activity. Climatic conditions and crop type also impact adoption of APVs. The study will help researchers and policy makers in developing long term strategies to create pathways for successful implementation and societal diffusion of agrivoltaics.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effects of Edge Sharpness of Triangular Prism-Shaped Plasmonic Nanoparticles on Confining Light to Improve the Opto-Electronic Performance of Thin Film Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)

authors.preferredName: A. F. M. Afnan Uzzaman Sheikh

abstract: This study uses computational techniques to investigate how the sharpness of edges on plasmonic metal nanoparticles (NPs), specifically triangular prisms, affects their light scattering and confining abilities in nanoscale regions. Various orientations of NPs were studied to assess their capability to confine light on the absorbing layer of silicon thin-film solar cells (TFSCs), thus investigating the possibility of enhancing the opto-electronic performance of the TFSCs. Optical data for different orientations of the NPs were obtained, and parameters such as the sharpness of the NPs were varied to investigate their correlation with maximizing the short circuit current density (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf>). The highest value for Jsc was found for opposing triangular aluminum prisms having a corner radius of 35nm that displayed a J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf> enhancement of over 50% compared to bare Si TFSC. The results indicate that more rounded edges in plasmonic NPs are suited to enhance the opto-electronic performance of TFSCs.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis of Market Clearing Price in the Indian Electricity Market Using Time Series Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: His paper investigates the effectiveness of four advanced time series forecasting models-LSTM., SARIMA, XGBoost, and Facebook Prophet-in predicting market-clearing prices in the dynamic Indian electricity market. Addressing the challenge of forecasting with voluminous and nonlinear data, this study employs diverse methodologies, from statistical to deep learning techniques, to capture temporal dependencies. Utilizing a comprehensive dataset from the IEX (India Energy Exchange Limited), which encompasses approximately 98% of the traded volume, these models are applied to weekly, monthly, and yearly data. Through extensive hyperparameter tuning and data preprocessing, each model's performance is assessed, highlighting specific strengths and limitations. This comparative analysis offers insights into selecting the most suitable model based on data characteristics, with implications for enhancing forecasting accuracy in volatile markets.

articleTitle: Optimizing Pakistan's Power Grid: A Study on EV Charging Infrastructure Potential
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The growing concerns over environmental pollution and decreasing fossil fuel reserves have made the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) grow each day. The biggest challenge in the penetration of EVs is the development of stable and user-friendly charging infrastructures. This work discusses the possibility and capacity of the existing power system to supply the electric vehicle charging infrastructure. First, a critical comparison of various charging schemes has been performed for the current scenario of Pakistan. An optimal charging scheme and a charging model, comprising public parking lots dedicatedly fed from the sub-transmission grid, are proposed. This model would be able to accommodate a large number of EVs for charging and smoothen the load curve of the utility with the proper coordination. The Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS) Lahore parking lot and corresponding grid station's load data have been taken as a reference to demonstrate the results. The results presented are shown to be beneficial both for EV consumers and for utility.

articleTitle: Wave Powered Desalination Systems - Recent Developments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: In remote offshore communities in discrete islands, the availability of potable water poses significant challenges. Several efforts are there to give them water in sustainable ways. Among the renewable energy resources, marine energy is the one that is a viable solution to generate or produce the needs of the potable water demands. The islands are surrounded by vast ocean water; many have abundant access to ocean wave energy sources nearby. This review paper explores the potential methods of wave-powered based desalination technologies. A review of existing systems with ample patents, research articles, and laboratory experiments have been conducted on marine energy systems. The main objective is to explore the existing systems and devices worldwide, identify suitable wave energy devices for Indian islands and seashore communities to maximize desalinated water production in island and seashore communities, and identify and determine the optimal specific energy consumption rates. Furthermore, this paper explores other advanced renewable technologies in research and their integration with desalination systems. Wave-powered desalination is still being researched to provide optimal solutions for integrating desalination units. This will highlight the technological advancements of existing systems and the challenges wave-powered desalination systems face.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Forecasting of Carbon Emissions in Thailand using Bayesian Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The global concern regarding climate change has centered around reducing CO2 emissions. Precise carbon emission forecasts are vital, as they allow policymakers, businesses, and individuals to make informed decisions about reducing emissions and transitioning to a low-carbon economy. This paper introduces a long-term probabilistic forecast of Thailand's carbon emissions using Bayesian deep neural networks. The model uses Gross Domestic Product, population, energy consumption, oil consumption, electricity generation and renewable energy generation as input parameters. The model is evaluated using the historical dataset from the Energy Policy and Planning Office, Ministry of Energy, Thailand, from 1990 to 2023. The impacts of increasing renewable energy generation, energy consumption, and oil consumption on carbon emissions are also evaluated.

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in the Energy Sector: A Comprehensive Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) enhances productivity by creating data, forecasting, optimizing, and understanding human language. In the energy sector, it is projected to have a $240 billion global economic impact, though research remains limited. This paper reviews GenAI's benefits, challenges, and research gaps in the energy sector, also focusing on climate change efforts. A PRISMA-SCR-based literature review from January 2022 to May 2024 was conducted using IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, ACM Digital Library, and Google Scholar. GenAI tools extracted data, verified by researchers. Analysis of 33 papers shows GenAI excels in knowledge integration and prediction. It generates synthetic electricity demand data, manages grids, forecasts energy demand, and optimizes renewable energy systems. Key challenges include hallucinations, data biases, privacy concerns, misuse, and system errors. Solutions involve improving training data, system fine-tuning, human oversight, and security measures. Research gaps include synthetic data realism, model evaluation standards, and integrating GenAI with blockchain and IoT.

articleTitle: A Scenario Based Multicriteria Analysis of Green Hydrogen as Transport Fuel in India: Studying the Socio-Economic-Environmental Dimensions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This study is based on three of the scenarios, of the India Energy Outlook 2021, the Stated Policy Scenario (STEPS); India Vision Case (IVC) and the Sustainable Development Scenario (SDS). The paper estimates the amount of green hydrogen (GH) that can be produced from renewable energy for each scenario and compares the economic, environmental and social impact of producing GH and using it as transport fuel replacing gasoline. The Multicriteria analysis consists of two parts, in the first part we consider the case where the entire projected renewable energy production in the three scenarios is used in generation of (GH) and in the second case we consider the impact of using a part of the renewable energy to meet electricity demand that is unmet by conventional power sources and use the excess renewable power to generate green hydrogen.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on Renewable Energy Revolution in India
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: India, a country home to 1.4 billion people and the world's fastest-growing major economy, lives in a state of uncertainty in terms of energy development. The purpose of this review paper is to appraise the change in energy status from the fossil-centric energy to Renewable Energy in case of India in light of mechanical development, increased urbanization, and favorable policies. India currently has an installed capacity of over 400,000 MW out of which around 179,000 MW is from renewable sources. They have planned to achieve 500 GW of non-fossil fuel installed capacity by 2030 and achieve net zero carbon emission target by 2070. Besides, the issues of intermittency and grid integration concerns, the Indian government has given immense importance to Renewable Energy, proving its pivotal role in spearheading the transition to a sustainable future - and provides the case studies that are valuable for enlightening those in bureaucracy, entrepreneurship, and academics.

articleTitle: Thermal Behavior and Optimization in Biomass Pyrolysis: A Modeling and Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The International Energy Agency recognizes that plant-derived lignocellulosic biomass can supply 10% of global clean, renewable energy. Pyrolysis, a thermochemical process converting biomass into biofuel, bio-chemicals, bio-char, and bio-oil under low oxygen, is crucial. This study focuses on developing mathematical models to understand biomass's thermal behaviour during pyrolysis at various temperatures and reaction rates. It reviews existing knowledge, identifies research gaps, and integrates biomass pyrolysis models. The findings align with previous experiments, noting that optimal heating rates minimize pyrolysis time. Recent advancements include using machine learning to reduce computational demands. The paper also briefly discusses the factors, limitations, and challenges of biomass pyrolysis.

articleTitle: Variable Renewable Energy Forecasting in the Philippines: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The Philippines is advancing its renewable energy goals to achieve a 35% share by 2030. This study evaluates solar photovoltaic (PV), and wind power output forecasting methods currently employed in the Philippines, aiming to assess their accuracy against electricity market standards and identify potential improvements. The study systematically reviews articles emphasizing forecasting methods, including physical, statistical, machine learning, and hybrid models. The methodologies encompass a range of forecasting horizons and utilize a diverse set of input variables that influence forecasting accuracy. A key finding from the literature is the variability in the accuracy of these forecasting models, with many not meeting the stringent Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) threshold of 18% set by the Philippines' Wholesale Electricity Spot Market (WESM). This emphasizes the need for enhanced forecasting models to mitigate economic losses and improve grid stability significantly. Furthermore, this study suggests integrating more sophisticated, data-driven forecasting models to improve accuracy. Such advancements are critical for managing the intermittent nature of solar and wind energy and making informed decisions on energy policy and investment in the Philippines. The study also identifies gaps in current forecasting practices and recommends avenues for future research, particularly in developing models that align better with the operational standards and real-time demands of the energy market.

articleTitle: Investigating Energy End-Use Efficiency in Small and Medium Scale Enterprises for Sustainable Industrialization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Industrial policies in Africa seem silent on energy efficiency measures for small and medium scale enterprises (SMEs) in the continent. Existing literature indicates that SMEs in Nigeria are unaware of energy end-use efficiency. Towards identifying policies for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 7, 9, and 13, energy end-use efficiency issues within one hundred (100) manufacturing SMEs were empirically analyzed.
