Probability Proportional to Size (PPS) technique was used to select the firms based on recent framing of enterprises by the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN). The study utilized structured questionnaires and interviews to capture cross-sectional data. The research identified some enablers of energy end-use efficiency in the companies. Factors identified equipment/appliance selection, capital and financial incentives, information and technical capacity, management commitment, smart manufacturing, and government policy or legislation. Contrary to the view in existing studies, the outcome of the study shows a strong awareness of energy end-use efficiency among 93.81% of the sampled firms. We recommend the roles of relevant stakeholders and some strategic measures essential for the improvement of energy end-use efficiency in SMEs towards decarbonizing the industrial sector and achieving sustainable development.

articleTitle: Analyzing Foreign Aid Research Trends in Energy: A Scientometric Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Billions of people worldwide lack access to basic energy services, relying on non-renewable sources like fossil fuels and traditional biomass. Given the energy challenges in many developing countries, foreign aid in the energy sector is crucial for reducing poverty, improving quality of life, and addressing climate change. This article presents a scientometric analysis using the Web of Science and Scopus databases to identify articles on energy-related foreign aid from the Rio Conference in 1992 to 2024. It examines trends, shifts in research focus, and the thematic and conceptual structures within the field, offering insights into its current and future trajectory. The results of the analysis are as follows: (1) China, as a provider of foreign aid, and the African continent, as a recipient of aid, are the most studied geographical areas. (2) Collaboration between researchers, institutions, and regions is weak, and publications in the field are scattered across numerous journals, hindering knowledge circulation and the emergence of new research clusters. (3) Although foreign aid in the energy sector has been a continuously growing research topic since 2019, numerous research gaps remain. Notably absent from the clusters are specific categories of energy, detailed analyses of various aid actors such as NGOs and civil society organizations, small-scale financial instruments like microfinance, other funding sources such as FDI, and new forms of cooperation, such as triangular cooperation between traditional donors and partners in the Global South.

articleTitle: Empowering Energy Transition: Detecting Cyber Threats in EV Charging Infrastructure through ML and XAI Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: With the adoption and usage levels on a newer scale in modern society, there is also equal effort or attention given to technological improvements for electric vehicle infrastructure and the EV Charging Network. With electric vehicles becoming more and more pervasive in number, there has been an even greater need to secure the EV charging networks and ensure they are safe from problems such as energy theft from the networks. However, most of these traditional security protocols cannot adapt to the ever-evolving landscape of cyber-attacks against electric vehicle chargers. With the outlined challenges, this research work aims to propose a Machine Learning-based approach in conjunction with the use of Explainable Artificial Intelligence to be capable of detecting various kinds of cyber-attacks, including DoS and advanced firmware modifications. The XAI brings together and ensures clarity in the models. XAI provides explanations about the details behind the much-needed opacity in how machine-learning models work and provides the understanding and confidence required by stakeholders and regulators that security will be deployed. It works to heighten cybersecurity not only in EV charging networks but also toward the general vision of creating resilient smart cities. It will help in developing confidence in and belief about the fast-evolving world of electric vehicle infrastructure.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Energy System Modeling Approaches for Decarbonizing the Electricity Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Comparative analysis is crucial for evidence-based decision-making for sustainable energy transitions. Identifying the strengths and weaknesses of various approaches is necessary before application. This review article presents a comparative analysis of energy system modeling approaches applied in the literature to develop decarbonization pathways for the electricity sector. The six most widely used applications are analyzed: TIMES/MARKAL, PyPSA, EnergyRT, SWITCH, OSeMOSYS, LEAP, and TIMES. SWOT analysis evaluates the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats of these models when applied toward net zero electricity systems by midcentury. PyPSA and Switch models emerge as top choices in analyzing the decarbonized future electricity sector due to adaptability, stakeholder compatibility, and policy alignment. The study aids researchers and policymakers in selecting an appropriate modeling approach by considering the strengths and limitations of each modeling technique. Furthermore, it underscores the necessity of ongoing evaluation and refinement to meet the evolving needs of the energy sector effectively, especially with the development of a new generation of open-source non-proprietary models.

articleTitle: Application of Grasshopper Optimization Algorithm for Design and Development of Net Zero Energy Residential Building in Ahmedabad, India
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This paper aims at applying Grasshopper-Optimization-Algorithm (GOA) for designing and developing a Net-Zero-Energy residential-building for a mega-city like Ahmedabad in India. The methodology implemented includes advanced tools like Revit for model creation and MATLAB for simulation, enabling the optimization of the building design. Leveraging detailed climatic data for Ahmedabad, Gujarat, and specific building parameters, the study effectively enhanced energy efficiency. GOA has been applied in reducing cooling loads and overall energy consumption through optimized passive design features. The findings highlight the significance of targeted optimization in building design for substantial energy savings and improved thermal performance. Furthermore, integrating solar panels significantly decreased energy consumption, with initial reductions from 9330 to 840 kWh. Subsequent MATLAB optimization further lowered consumption to 37.558 kWh per month, primarily during peak energy demand months of April to July. This endeavor aimed to achieve near-zero-energy consumption, showcasing the potential of renewable energy integration in building sustainability.

articleTitle: Stability Assessment of Utility Grids with Integration of Large Decentralized Variable Renewable Energy Sources- A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The recent surge in electricity demand has been accompanied by a substantial increase in the grid integration of large decentralized variable renewable energy resources. This influx, while promising for sustainable energy, poses challenges such as reduced inertia, diminished short circuit contributions, and heightened stability issues. This paper highlights the intricate interaction between solar inverters and the network utilities, aiming to propose mitigation methods that enhance the stability of future power systems. The study covers both steady state and dynamic conditions, considering different inverter modes of operation, such as voltage control, reactive power control, and power factor control. The conditions have been simulated comprehensively, modeling all specified parameters at both the inverter and plant levels. Dynamic models have been finetuned to ensure compliance with grid code requirements at the plant level. However, the final updated model must undergo validation using site-specific measurements, integrating actual field data into the final assessment.

articleTitle: Economic Analysis Framework for Climate Adaptation Investment Towards Resilient Land Transport Infrastructure with a Thailand Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Recent global climate commitment emphasizes the necessity of climate-proofing investments in land transport infrastructure. Such investments are typically substantial and require thorough economic analysis. This paper introduces a systematic economic framework that includes Total Investment Estimation (TIE) which bridges Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) and Investment and Financial Flow (I&FF) assessment. TIE classifies target areas, categorizes countermeasures, and prioritizes investment decisions. A case study of Thailand's land transport sector was used to demonstrate the usability of the framework. Stakeholders can use this framework to develop economically feasible and affordable climate-proofing investment strategies.

articleTitle: Changes in Transport Demand and Modal Shift on GHG Emissions in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Thailand's economic success relies heavily on its transportation infrastructure, which is a major contributor to GHG emissions. To address these challenges, Thailand has developed transportation infrastructure plan focused on enhancing its transport system, promoting mass transit, and adopting advanced technologies to reduce energy consumption and GHG emissions. This study developed a transport demand model for Thailand to estimate future demand and to assess the impact of behavioral changes on modal shifts, considering mode-specific costs. The transport demand model was then linked with the AIM/Enduse to analyze long-term energy consumption and GHG emissions pathways. Scenarios, including reference, COVID, and transport modal shift policy, estimate significant impacts from changes in behavior and a shift to mass transit on energy use and GHG emissions. By prioritizing public transport infrastructure, Thailand will substantially increase its transport demand, however, energy consumption and GHG emissions will decrease by 23.1% and 22.0% in 2060 compared to reference scenario.

articleTitle: Analysis of Adoption Rates and Planning of Residential Prosumers based on Solar Rooftops PV
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The growing adoption of solar rooftop PV in residential sectors is transforming energy consumption patterns and driving the rise of electricity prosumers. This study focuses on analyzing the adoption rates and strategic planning for residential prosumers in Thailand, with an emphasis on solar rooftop PV systems. Utilizing the Bass Diffusion Model, a market penetration curve was developed to forecast the adoption of residential prosumers, incorporating an innovation coefficient of 0.03. Key factors such as economic incentives, solar irradiance, installation costs, and government policies were integrated into the forecasting model, enabling a comprehensive assessment of prosumer adoption trends. The findings suggest that regions with higher solar potential and robust government incentives are likely to see faster growth in residential prosumers, while areas with less favorable policy environments will experience slower adoption rates. This trend aligns with previous studies, which have highlighted similar patterns in other regions globally. Behavioral and technological factors, including environmental awareness and advancements in PV technology and ESS, further enhance adoption rates. However, the increasing number of residential prosumers introduces significant challenges for grid stability and management. This study also highlights the importance of smart grid technology due to the growing number of distributed energy sources. It calls for the utilization of AI models for load forecasting and demand response mechanisms to ensure the efficient integration of prosumers into the utility grid. In particular, regions with high concentrations of prosumers may require targeted policies to maintain grid reliability and address the technical complexities posed by distributed generation. This research provides a dynamic analysis of residential prosumer adoption and offers strategic recommendations for energy planners and policymakers. It emphasizes the importance of incentives, technological advancements, and effective grid management to foster energy sustainability and empower citizens in Thailand's energy transition. The results also offer a framework for similar regions globally to plan and manage the growth of residential prosumers, ensuring that energy transitions are effective, sustainable, and beneficial for all stakeholders involved.

articleTitle: Enhancing Biogas Purification Efficiency Through Microbial Intervention: A Comparative Analysis of Carbon Dioxide and Hydrogen Sulfide Removal in Anaerobic Digestion Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Biogas purification remains a significant challenge in renewable energy production. This study investigates the application of Effective Microorganisms (EM) for biogas refinement, focusing on the removal of carbon dioxide (CO2) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S). A novel experimental setup utilizing polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles was designed to produce and purify biogas. The system incorporated an anaerobic digester, raw biogas storage, and purification components including shock dose and maintenance dose reactors containing EM solutions at various concentrations (1%, 5%, and 10%). Over a 60-day period, biogas production and purification were monitored. Results showed that the 10% EM setup consistently demonstrated the highest removal efficiency for CO2 and H2S, followed by the 5% and 1% EM setups. The control setup using water scrubbing exhibited decreasing efficiency over time. While the control setup achieved the highest methane concentration in purified biogas (78.94<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>), the EM setups showed superior performance in removing impurities. The study highlights the tradeoff between impurity removal and methane retention, emphasizing the need to balance these factors for optimal biogas quality and energy efficiency. The EM setups also influenced methane production patterns, with peak production occurring after an initial 13-day growth phase. This research contributes to our understanding of microbial interventions in biogas refinement and their implications for improved biogas production and purification. The findings could have significant implications for developing sustainable, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly biogas refinement technologies, particularly for small-scale and household applications.

articleTitle: Forecasting Indian Conventional Generation: A Comparative Analysis of ARIMA and SARIMA Models for Improved Energy Demand Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This research presents an efficient approach to anticipate future conventional electricity generation, offering valuable insights into addressing upcoming energy demands. To unified models are introduced, Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) and Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), tailored for predicting India's conventional electricity generation. This model is trained over a 40-month dataset and is sourced from the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), which utilizes autocorrelation and partial correlation plots to determine the optimal model order. Among these models, SARIMAX demonstrates superior accuracy over ARIMA, selected based on lower values of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values. Using Machine Learning Algorithms, the current conventional trends can be analyzed, and effective methods can be employed to sustain stability in the power system grids in India. The models provide valuable insights into forthcoming load patterns and projected electricity demands by the year 2031.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Based Forecasting Models for Solar PV/Hydrogen Fuel Cell Power System: Role of Short-Term AI-Based Forecasting for the Energy Transition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This study aims to assess the viability of using solar photovoltaic (PV) water electrolyzer to generate green hydrogen and sustainable energy, with the specific goal of meeting the electrical demands of buildings in arid locations. Models for short-term ANN power output predictions from solar PV and fuel cells, as well as green hydrogen production, are developed. By utilizing a power system fueled exclusively by renewable resources and zero-carbon fuels, our objective is to build a structure that operates without consuming fossil fuel energy. Modeling, simulation, and optimization analysis were used in this study to evaluate the system's technical, economic, and environmental performance. The artificial neural network (ANN) prediction models utilize simulated input and output data to forecast the production of hydrogen through solar-powered electrolyzer. The building's daily, monthly, and annual electricity demands were all fulfilled by the self-sufficient hybrid solar PV/fuel cell power system. The hybrid power system being proposed generates 79.7% and 20.3% of its electricity from solar photovoltaic (PV) and fuel cell sources, respectively. The electrolyzer requires an energy input of 898,415 kilowatt-hours, produces 19,360 kilograms of hydrogen, and consumes 15,817 kilograms of hydrogen for the fuel cell per year. The mean and maximum output of the electrolyzer for green hydrogen production are 2.21 and 10.8 kg/hr., respectively, with a specific energy of 46.4 kWh/kg. The training, validation, and test R values for solar PV power output and green hydrogen production, obtained from the ANN-based forecasting models, range from 0.967 to 0.974 and from 0.981 to 0.982, respectively. The correlation coefficient R and mean square errors MSE of the ANN regression model indicate that the models provide accurate estimations of the power output of solar PV systems and the production of green hydrogen by electrolyzer.

articleTitle: Sustainable Design and Community Engagement: Lessons Learned from Low-Carbon Communities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This paper examines sustainable design features and community engagement mechanisms in selected low-carbon residential communities, aiming to understand better and implement these strategies. The research selects specific communities and collects and analyzes data from various sources. The main findings show that energy-efficient building designs, renewable energy utilization, safety and security, social activities, and mobility and transportation are common features in low-carbon communities. However, less attention is paid to strategic economic development. Successful low-carbon communities need clear communication and stakeholder engagement. Challenges include high construction and maintenance costs, communication and knowledge sharing, and better integration of green technologies. This study provides practical suggestions and highlights the importance of early-stage participation in strategic planning, design, and operation for achieving sustainability goals.

articleTitle: Redefining Energy Economics: A Comprehensive Analysis of Negative Pricing Phenomenon
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Negative Pricing of Electricity has emerged as a consequential economic phenomenon wherein the surplus supply of electricity surpasses demand, leading to the unprecedented situation where the price of electricity plummets below zero. This paper examines the multidimensional nature of this phenomenon. It delves into the underlying causes fuelling its rise and investigates the proactive measures undertaken by key stakeholders such as generating companies (GENCOs) and governmental bodies to address this challenge. Drawing insights from diverse global contexts, including the United States, Germany, Australia, and Denmark, the paper presents an in-depth analysis of four distinct scenarios. It elucidates the specific strategies adopted in each region to mitigate the adverse effects of negative pricing, shedding light on both successes and limitations. Furthermore, the paper explores promising technological advancements poised to revolutionize the energy landscape and potentially alleviate the prevalence of negative pricing. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of the complexities surrounding this phenomenon while offering valuable insights for policymakers, industry professionals, and researchers alike. By synthesizing empirical evidence and forward-looking perspectives, this paper aims to stimulate discourse and foster innovative solutions toward achieving a more resilient and sustainable energy ecosystem.

articleTitle: PyPSA-BD: An Open-Source Model for Planning Sustainable Power Sector for Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The necessity of decarbonizing the power sector has become central to achieving sustainable development goals on a global scale. Despite its significance, the application of electricity sector modeling remains limited, especially in developing nations such as Bangladesh. This study aims to bridge this gap by utilizing open data and open-source code to conduct a comprehensive analysis of Bangladesh's power system transition up to 2050. Specifically, Python for Power System Analysis (PyPSA) is employed to develop a customized model named PyPSA-BD. Leveraging ERA5 reanalyses data, we construct cost-optimized models that consider various national policies, with particular emphasis on pivotal years such as 2030, 2041, and 2050. Through a comparative analysis with official reports from the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB), Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB), and Integrated Energy and Power Master Plan (IEPMP) 2023, this research sheds light on key insights crucial for policy formulation, effective management, and strategic investment planning within Bangladesh's power sector.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Framework for Optimizing Multi-Period EV Charging Infrastructure Deployment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The rise of electric vehicles represents a transformative shift in the automotive industry, signaling the dawn of a new era of clean, sustainable transportation, but their operation requires a distributed rapid-charging infrastructure. Building such rapid charging networks is currently capital-intensive and therefore, requires careful planning and the development of the charging infrastructure must be maintained. However, infrastructure construction is not a one-off investment but a multi-period plan. A multi-period location and capacity expansion model of the charging stations will be needed. This study proposes a novel data-driven framework for deploying suitable rapid-charging infrastructure for EVs in large urban areas. This study combines an iterative clustering technique with a geographical information system analysis tool to determine the suitable regions for developing an optimized EV charging service. The analysis intends to plan a case study for Gurugram City of India and suggest the locations that should be the potential points for consideration of charging station development.

articleTitle: A Review of the Battery Safety, Protection and Disposal Standards in India
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: In the process of achieving the Government of India's five-element plan (Panchamrit) to combat climate change, the transport sector is undergoing drastic changes. In parallel to enhancing and encouraging the electric vehicle (EV) ecosystem in India, it is equally important and pertinent to focus on the safety aspects of batteries. The rise in the mass production of these batteries and the increased consumer demand will significantly exacerbate the problems and safety aspects associated with the operation, maintenance, recovery, recycling and disposal of batteries. In this paper, EVs (passenger carriers) available in the Indian market, along with the battery type and charging times, are explored and presented. Also, an overview of the regulatory mechanism governing the automobile industry in India is described. The automotive industry standards in India developed under the Central Motor Vehicle Rules (CMVR) are also discussed. Some popular and dominant International and National standards development bodies/organizations are listed. Applications of lithium batteries and the potential hazards they pose if mishandled or improperly manufactured are mentioned. UN 38.3 - testing requirements and criteria for safely transporting lithium batteries are outlined. Importantly, (IS) 16046, developed by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) was analysed and discussed in detail. The battery disposal mechanism in India, governed by the battery waste management rules, is incorporated. Finally, recommendations were provided to strengthen the existing standards.

articleTitle: Sustainability in the Global Food Systems with Synergies and Trade-Offs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Sustainability in the global food system is a pressing matter. Healthy and nutritious diet should have minimum environmental footprints, it is a highly debatable topic that food scientists, local farmers, food manufacturers, private sector and governments regularly plan round-tables to dictate new policies. However, one or more party usually oppose the new policies, which is the major conundrum of Sustainable Diet within Global food system. This paper deals with Sustainable Diet Notions, tackling food waste and agro-waste, understanding different supply chains in the food system and how circular economy should be effectively implemented. Multiple innovative approaches are introduced from multidisciplinary and circular economy perspectives to: a. Reduce carbon footprints, b. Save resources and huge economic burden of waste control, c. Provide an idea for a new possible merging market based on eco-friendly technology, d. Significantly reduce food waste, e. Significantly reduce food insecurity, hunger and hidden hunger.

Author Keywords: -• Circular Economy• Food Insecurity• Food waste • GHG emissions • Sustainable Diet

articleTitle: Deep Eutectic Solvent Pretreatment of Pineapple Peel for Enhanced Cellulose Conversion: Towards Sustainable Biofuel Production
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Given the substantial cellulose content in pineapple fruit peel, redirecting this waste towards second-generation biofuel production could significantly diminish the need for environmentally taxing on-field handling practices. The objective of this study was to investigate the potential of the fruit peel as a substitute cellulose source by analyzing its chemical composition. A pretreatment method utilizing Deep Eutectic Solvent (DES), a green solvent, which is composed of a blend of ethylene glycol and citric acid, was employed. The results revealed that the glucose and xylose content increased to 59.85% and 97.12%, respectively, after pretreatment. The total reducing sugar present in the untreated and pretreated samples was 0.057 g/g and 0.095 g/g respectively. Furthermore, an assessment of chemical structural alterations in the biomass was conducted to verify the efficacy of pretreatment. Therefore, this study confirmed the potential of this biomass as a biorefinery feedstock and it is expected to produce more value-added products from it.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Carbon Accounting Methodologies and Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Global warming, driven by human activities increasing greenhouse gas levels, poses a significant threat. Rising temperatures, disrupted ecosystems, and extreme weather result. CO2 emissions impact the global climate system and various sectors. Carbon accounting helps assess emissions' origins and aids in mitigation. This study examines different carbon accounting methods, each with strengths, limitations and policy implications. Production Based Accounting (PBA) provides reliable data but neglects consumption patterns, potentially causing carbon leakage. Consumption-Based Accounting (CBA) offers a comprehensive view but faces challenges in data collection and political support. Input Output Analysis (IOA) integrates production and consumption but has uncertainties. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) evaluates environmental impacts from production to disposal but needs extensive data. Household Income Expenditure Survey (HIES) highlights emissions differences by income level for fair policies. Combining these methods is crucial for effective climate mitigation. Each approach has implications for policy-making: PBA for reliable data, solely assigns responsibility to production locations CBA for broader perspective, requires political support for successful implementation, IOA for strategies, LCA for cleaner practices, and HIES for equitable policies.

articleTitle: Building Energy Performance Benchmarking: Current Methods, Applications, and Implications for the Philippines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This paper reviews the current methods used in building energy performance benchmarking (BEPB), focusing on statistical models, physical models, machine learning, and hybrid approaches. It synthesizes findings from 45 studies, identifying the common variables such as gross floor area, occupancy, and electricity consumption used to benchmark energy performance across various building types, including residential, schools, and offices. The paper discusses the potential applicability of these methods in the Philippine context, emphasizing the need for region-specific benchmarks and improved data collection infrastructure. The study concludes that hybrid approaches, which combine statistical and machine learning methods, hold the greatest potential for enhancing energy efficiency in the Philippines, given that challenges related to data availability and technical expertise are addressed.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Applications in Wave Energy Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Wave energy derived from oceanic kinetic forces is a highly promising renewable energy source. As global efforts to incorporate renewable energy into the grid increase, accurate wave energy forecasting becomes essential for optimizing energy harvesting and grid integration. This paper examines the latest developments in machine learning (ML) approaches, focusing on deep learning (DL), ensemble methods, and hybrid models used for forecasting ocean wave energy. It highlights the strengths and weaknesses of various approaches in capturing the complex nonlinear dynamics of ocean waves, including predicting energy flux, significant wave height (SWH), and wave period. Additionally, the paper explores how hybrid models, combining physical models with ML, have emerged as powerful tools for improving forecast accuracy over traditional methods. This review concludes with insights into future directions, emphasizing the potential of advanced techniques like transformers, generative adversarial networks (GANs), and real-time data assimilation for enhancing prediction reliability and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: External Interlinkages Between SDGs, Clean Energy, and COVID-19: a Systematic Review of Policy Framework and Goals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Despite the wealth of studies on SDGs interlinkages, the energy sector, as one of the agenda, is solely illustrated in distinct indicators and targets under SDG 7. On the other hand, energy is one of the most vulnerable sectors impacted by the COVID-19 that could trigger sustainability crisis by possible failure to follow the net zero scenarios. The analysis on the relationship between SDGs and clean energy during the pandemic is considered necessary as it has challenged the revisions of nationally climate-change based initiatives and policy agenda at the country level. This study conducts a systematic review to elaborate the synergies between SDGs and existing energy related policy options and fills the knowledge gap on how those interactions during the COVID-19 bring a major influence to sustainability policy-making at the global level. The result is expected to appear as measurable energy-related policy options to deal with global health-system crisis in the future.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of PM KUSUM Scheme Individual Pump Solar Component C
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Utthaan Maha Abhiyaan (PM KUSUM) Scheme, launched by the government of India, allows for the availability of solar-powered agricultural pumps at subsidized rates to farmers of the country. The scheme's Individual Pump Solar (IPS) Component C intends to use grid-connected solar pumps. This way, the farmer saves money on the electricity he would have bought from the grid and generates an income by selling the surplus energy back to the grid. This would create a parallel revenue stream for the farmers while saving up simultaneously. This paper probes the impact of the PM KUSUM Scheme, especially component C, on the environmental and economic front. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) has released a list of the number of pumps allocated to various states in the country under the PM KUSUM Scheme. MNRE has also released a price list of the pumps the farmers can buy. Using this list and calculated projection of pump categorization, purchase cost estimates have been made in this paper, which would later be used to calculate the time period for Return on Investment (ROI). Using the available annual daylight hours and the average time, the farmers would use the pump to irrigate the fields; energy savings have been calculated. The energy saved here refers to the amount of electrical power the farmer would have taken from the grid but instead met his demands with the solar pump. The electricity produced is sold back to the grid during the remaining period, and the income generated is calculated. Since generation capacity changes over time, the projected power mix was calculated for analysis. Furthermore, year-wise, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions saved were also calculated. These calculations are used to estimate carbon credits saved annually by the country to give a better perspective of this scheme's impact. Calculations show average annual carbon credit savings from 2026 onwards (after the full implementation) worth INR 307 million and about 114,935 metric tonnes worth of annual CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission savings, and an ROI period of 1 year and nine months for the farmers.

articleTitle: Exploring the Prospect of Digital Tracking Technology in Enhancing the Circularity of the Swedish Precast Concrete Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: This study investigates the drivers and barriers to adopting Digital Tracking Technologies (DTT) for enhancing circularity in the Swedish precast concrete sector. Utilising a mixed-method design, it combines quantitative text analytics of social media posts, generating word clouds and sentiment analysis, with thematic analysis of stakeholder interviews. These interviews are analysed through a PESTLE framework, mapped to SWOT, and further examined using the Multi-Level Perspective (MLP) framework to understand transitional dynamics across the: ‘niche,’ ‘regime,’ and ‘landscape’ levels. The analysis identified 22 drivers and 24 barriers to DTT adoption, emphasising the critical role of regulatory frameworks, technological innovations, and industry practices in promoting DTT for circular economy (CE) purposes. The findings offer valuable insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders, guiding further exploration and decision-making in this field.

articleTitle: Biofuel from Forest Tree Species: Challenges and Opportunities in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: The government of Indonesia has a clear target to reduce fossil fuel which will be replaced by renewable sources. In meeting its energy demand, reducing reliance on fossil fuel, import and complying with national as well as global commitments for emission reduction, the Government of Indonesia passed mixed energy policies and regulations. It particularly used palm oils as one renewable biodiesel resources. However, concerns over food security and deforestation have arisen recently. On the other hands, there is huge potential in native forest tree species that would produce high yield and non-edible oils. The country's extensive degraded lands amounting to 12.7 million hectares offer an opportunity to develop forest energy plantations while restoring the lands and ecosystems. This review elaborates on the country's biofuel development and its potential for energy transition based on forest tree species using SWOT analysis. We found that implementation of blending policies in Indonesia which tend to be accelerated is favourable for developing non-edible oil for biofuels. Calophyllum inophyllum and Pongamia pinnata have a huge potential to be further developed for plantations. Further research is needed to deeply analyze feedstock capacities, breeding strategies, and promote aviation fuels from forest tree species, making its production cost financially feasible.

articleTitle: Effect of Energy Efficiency and Conservation Towards Net-Zero
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Sustainable Energy: Energy Transition and Net-Zero Climate Future (ICUE)
abstract: In India, the Energy Conservation Act 2001 was notified on 29<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> September 2001 to incentivize the efficient use of energy and its conservation. Emphasis was placed on awareness within all the sections of society, prioritizing specific high energy-consuming sectors like industries, agriculture, municipals, buildings, and the domestic sector. These sectors are governed by programs and regulations like Perform Achieve & Trade, Agriculture Demand Side Management, Municipal Demand Side Management, Energy Conservation Building Code, and Star Labelling Programme, through Bureau of Energy Efficiency. A case study of Chhattisgarh State about the awareness creation has supported the implementation of energy efficiency measures, has been considered to evaluate journey of high energy-consuming sectors to become energy efficient, leading to achieve net zero utilizing Solar Energy. In two decades, energy consumption reduced by 2.7 million units through government initiatives resulting in avoided capacity of 1280MW in the industrial sector. Efficient Energy Transition will ease the journey to Net-Zero.
